newsitem.title: MEXICO: Venezuela moves to solve Latam sugar spat - source.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela moves to solve Latam sugar spat - source.

text.p: Venezuela and Latin American sugar exporters have reached a pre-accord to solve their regional sugar spat that stirred dipolmatic waters in recent months, a leading Veneuzuelan sugar industrialist said here Friday.

Venezuela will soon drop its temporary import ban and allow a total of 387,000 tonnes of raw sugar imports into the country from May, solving a rift between Caracas and the neighboring nations of Central America and Colombia, the source told Reuters, requesting anonymity.

Several months ago, Venezuela slapped a temporary import ban on sugar, claiming its domestic market was saturated. Central American nations, particularly El Salvador, slammed the move as protectionism and were forced to divert elsewhere their pending exports to Venezuela.

"We have reached a pre-accord that has been agreed in principle by both Colombia and Central America," the industrialist said here in southern Mexico. Sugar producers, traders and consumers had gathered for the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference.
Of the 387,000 tonnes to be allowed into Venezuela, Colombia has been earmarked 270,000 tonnes and 117,000 has been allocated to Central American producers to split among themselves.

"It is still not official but those are going to be the figures more or less," the industrialist said, stressing the accord was for raw sugar imports only and that Central American producers still had to decide how to divide up their allocation.

Premiums will be paid by Venezuela to Colombia and El Salvador, both with refining capacity to produce white sugar which fetches higher prices, on the raw exports they ship to Venezuela, the source added.
Venezuela government, in a bid to ease tensions with its neighbors, told its sugar associations and businessmen to sort out the import battle to remove the issue from the diplomatic table.

But Venezuela's powerful sugar lobby has insisted on raw sugar imports only to make use of its own refining capacity. "It does not make sense to import whites when we have the refineries standing idle," the industrialist added.

Venezuela's own 1996-1997 sugar harvest to end at 520,000 tonnes this October-April cycle, but with annual consumption hovering around 850,000 tonnes, the country has long been a net importer of sugar.
